name: Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the defection scene)
key_role: New hero of Karnataka — inherits the elephant-bond at the throne-stone's fall — destined Maha-Adhipati of Volume I
relationships: Twin brother of Bhoomi-Takshaka (deceased); cousin to Tungabhadra (deceased) and Krishnaveni (AP); foster-father to Hampi-of-the-Bronze and the Third Herald
notes: Bloodline-A heir who lived 36 years as his sister's silent court-architect; defects with the buried-temple blueprints; Yudhishthira-mapped (reluctant king); his name maps to the historical Krishnadevaraya.

name: Hampi-of-the-Bronze
introduced_in: Ch 1 references; first prose appearance Ch 2 Beat 1
key_role: Heir-presumptive of Karnataka; chosen ward of Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata; takes the Third Herald's hand at chapter's end
relationships: Orphan of the Chapter-1 temple-quake (grandmother was Bloodline-A noblewoman); raised by Tungabhadra from age 4; ward of Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata from Ch 2 end
notes: Ten years old. Brown-eyed and quiet. Reads people the way her foster-mother read battlefields. Will grow into a major figure across Ch 3 and Ch 4.

name: Veerappa-Hadali
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the walk to the forest-edge hamlet)
key_role: Symbolic 'king for one hour' who legitimises the destruction of the throne-stone; holds the Hadali veto over future imperial revivals
relationships: Eighty-three; never attended a Karnataka Council in seventy years until Tungabhadra walks to his hamlet alone
notes: His clan's vote is the moral hinge of Chapter Three's Unity Trial; the Hadali seat on the Karnataka Council is now permanent.

name: The Third Herald (Bronze-Dust Child)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue
key_role: The third of the Void Maw's four heralds; planted as the Karnataka-region Maw sign
relationships: The Bloodline-A infant 'swallowed' by the Chapter-1 temple-earthquake, now returned in the form a Herald takes; recognised as a Herald by Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata through the bond
notes: His true identity (Tungabhadra's forgotten cousin-son) is revealed in Chapter Four when Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata speaks his full lineage inside the Maw. Saga-rule established here: Heralds are remembered, not killed.

name: Ferreira-de-Sangam
faction: Mixed-tide (a new fourth-faction at chapter's end)
bloodline: E (through her mother's Pernem line; her paternal Portuguese ancestry is not Bloodline-bound)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Interval (the night she walks into Sagaradeva's hut)
key_role: Becomes the Goan resistance lead after Sagaradeva's death; will federate Goa under Gujarat's Western umbrella in Chapter Three; first non-Bloodline-pure leader of a fallen kingdom
relationships: Half-Portuguese (paternal line from a 1693 Old Goa shipwright), half-Goan (maternal Pernem family); refused by Sagaradeva; takes in the Second Herald and Padre Cordeiro the morning after the storm; receives the bird-message from Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata at midday
notes: Carries the dual heritage Sagaradeva would not. Speaks Konkani, Portuguese, English, Marathi. Does not carry the gaur-bond — the bond walks past her, north, to Shivagati. Carries the kingdom instead.

name: Bhau Tendulkar
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the net-mending scene at Querim)
key_role: Recites the 1873 promise to Sagaradeva at low tide; assassinated by port-consortium freighter mid-chapter; his death is the moment Sagaradeva commits fully to the Karna-shadow
relationships: Patriarch of the Tendulkar-line fishing villages; great-grandson of the man who originally extracted the promise from the Sagaravamsha; daughter Sona Tendulkar inherits leadership
notes: His killing is logged officially as 'visibility failure.' The investigation is filed in Panaji and never closed. The fishermen know what it was. Sagaradeva knows what it was. The keeping of the promise becomes inevitable after this.

name: Sona Tendulkar
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (her father's funeral)
key_role: Inherits leadership of the Tendulkar-line villages after her father's death; recovers Sagaradeva and Maha-Vega's bodies at Sinquerim; orders the brothers buried together in the same coastal grove
relationships: Daughter of Bhau Tendulkar; co-operator of the Sagara-Tantra Mk.I mesh-network into Ch 3; mother of two daughters who will appear in Chapter Three
notes: Her decision to bury Maha-Vega beside Sagaradeva is one of the saga's quietest dharmic acts. The fisherman-line refuses the easy purity. Her two daughters become major figures in Chapter Three's Maharashtra-Goa federation.

name: Padre Fernando Cordeiro
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the press conference; later resignation)
key_role: Initially the consortium's diplomatic face; resigns publicly the morning after the storm; walks to Ferreira-de-Sangam's house and asks for a place in the resistance
relationships: Goan-Catholic priest of Old Goa parish; recognises the Second Herald as a Herald (having read the Karnataka news); becomes operational steward of the Mauja-Drishti drone fleet
notes: Speaks Konkani, Portuguese, English, Italian. His resignation is the consortium's first major public defection. The press handle it as a 'cultural advisor's personal decision'; nobody is fooled, including the consortium.

name: Vasco-without-a-ship (The Second Herald)
bloodline: E (by hidden descent — Sagaravamsha-line sailor lost in 1731)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the morning after the storm)
key_role: The second of the Void Maw's four heralds; planted as the Goa-region Maw sign
relationships: Recognised as a Herald by Padre Cordeiro; taken in and named by Ferreira-de-Sangam; sits at her front step for a week before speaking his first three-word sentence
notes: Wears 17th-century sailor's clothing salt-stained but not aged. His shadow does not match the morning sun. True identity (revealed Ch 4): a Sagaravamsha-line sailor who was meant to be the line's heir before Sagaradeva's great-grandfather, lost at sea in 1731, forgotten when he returned — the forgetting itself is what the Void Maw has given a body. Per Karnataka's rule he is not killed; he is named.

name: Tanaji-the-Second
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (the wall-climb at the forty-sixth fort)
key_role: Saga's first follower-by-skill rather than by blood or contract; his half-kneel in the command-room is the established pattern for later 'voluntary follower' conversions across Ch 3
relationships: Descendant of a 17th-century commander who served at Sinhagad under the historical Tanaji Malusare; commands the forty-sixth fort (a small mid-ridge garrison silent on every council vote for thirty years); has three close fort-commander neighbours (Lohagad, Tikona, Visapur) whose conversion he triggers within a fortnight
notes: Fifty. Tea-drinking, four-hours-a-night sleeper, refuses to be photographed for any newspaper. His acceptance of Shivagati establishes the Wall-Climb Rite as a saga form — replicated (with variants) by Jagannath-Bandhu pulling the Rath Yatra chariot, Moirangthem dancing the disqualification dance, etc. In Ch 3 he becomes Maharashtra's de facto holder under Gujarat's Western federation umbrella. Survives Volume I.

name: Bhausaheb
introduced_in: Ch 1 (briefly referenced); Ch 2 Beat 3 (the visit to Pratapgad before the wall-climb plan)
key_role: Shivagati's closest non-Vanaraksha kin; Sinhagad fort-commander; brings Shivagati the wall-climb plan in the second-half pivot conversation
relationships: First cousin to Shivagati (their fathers were brothers); cousin Bhausaheb-the-First (deceased at sixteen in the Ch 1 spring battle) was his younger brother and is buried at the Murud-Janjira island-cemetery now under Dattaji Mohite's seizure
notes: Twelve years older than Shivagati. Operationally runs the Hariyal-Net mesh. Survives Ch 2. Per restructure §4 (not in the table but implied by Shivagati's death in Ch 3) he becomes Tanaji-the-Second's principal council voice when Maharashtra is absorbed under Gujarat — the older voice in the room.

name: The Burnt Squirrel-Nest (place-sign)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (week 6)
key_role: First place-based Maw sign in the chapter; precedent for non-herald Maw signs (an absence rather than a person)
relationships: Pilgrimage site by season's end; shrine built by Tanaji-the-Second at the base of the Sahyadri ironwood tree
notes: Mechanism: the Void Maw has read the Sahyadri and erased one Indian Giant Squirrel from the record. The carbonisation of the upper canopy is what remains when a creature's presence is removed without anything ever having been there to remove. Shivagati does not retaliate. The Karnataka rule holds. Maharashtra's contribution to the maw-signs catalogue is the first place-sign — establishes that the Maw appears in three forms across the chapter: people (Heralds), places (the burnt nest), and absence-of-things (later signs).

name: Yamunadatta
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the throne-room arrival)
key_role: Visible Maharaj of UP from the Imambara assembly onward; the North's throne-figure into Ch 3 and Ch 4
relationships: Son of Gangaputra and Radhika; nephew of Adharma (refuses political alignment); cousin to Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata of Karnataka and to Krishnaveni of AP; will accept his uncle Adharma into a council seat at Ch 3 Unity Trial
notes: Abhimanyu-mapped. Tall for fourteen, briefed thoroughly, composure beyond his years. Half-Bloodline-A through his mother gives him the cross-bond legitimacy that the Imambara settlement requires. His Stage IV ladder is the inheritance Gangaputra explicitly released to him. He will be the senior crown of the North Dominant Council in Ch 3 and a key voice at Kurukshetra in Ch 4.

name: Radhika
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the throne-room arrival)
key_role: The boy's mother; dharmic argument-source for acknowledgement; permanent third-party arbitration seat granted to her temple-circle in the Imambara settlement
relationships: Yamunadatta's mother; ex-lover (one autumn 2010) of Gangaputra; great-granddaughter of a Hampi noblewoman who migrated north to Vrindavan in 1875; returns to Vrindavan within a fortnight of the Imambara; visits her son every full moon
notes: Krishna-Radha tradition trained classical singer. Refused contact with Gangaputra for 14 years out of Krishna-cult teaching (the mother carries the silence until the child asks). Her dharmic absolutism is the moral pivot that gives Gangaputra the courage to abdicate rather than just legitimise. Survives Volume I. Her temple circle becomes the standing third-party arbitration-seat for personal-dharma matters in the North Dominant Council.

name: Vidura-Babu
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the throne-room scene)
key_role: UP's chief minister; drafts the Imambara settlement document; constitutional architect of the North Dominant federation in Ch 3
relationships: Long-serving Lucknow administrator; trusted by Gangaputra absolutely; works closely with Yamunadatta from week 2 onward as principal political tutor; survives Volume I
notes: Sixty-one. Handloom kurtas, rimless reading glasses, Awadhi-court trained. The Mahabharata's Vidura name evokes the wise minister who was usually ignored — but in this kingdom in this chapter, the Vidura IS heard. Stayed up the entire night before the Imambara with three legal scribes drafting the settlement. Becomes the kingdom's most reliable adult voice through the male-led restructure.

name: Mahaguru Drona-of-the-Plain
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (the Imambara testimony)
key_role: Official guru to Gangaputra, Kurukshetraa (Haryana), and Panchanada (Punjab); his Imambara testimony is the redemption arc of his 40-year debt to MP's Adharma-Kendra
relationships: Maternal uncle saved by Adharma-Kendra 40 years ago; Drona has tilted counsel toward Adharma-Kendra ever since; teacher to three North heroes; will be hunted by Adharma-Kendra into MP's Ch 2 civil war
notes: His Imambara testimony — straight, against the debt, for dharma — is one of the chapter's quietest pivots. Pays for it in MP's Ch 2 story (next session). Per the relationship-graph he carries the cross-kingdom secret across all four chapters. Survives into Ch 3 if he can outrun Adharma-Kendra's pursuit; flagged as uncertain into Ch 4.

name: The Clear Ganga (landscape-sign)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (morning after the Imambara)
key_role: First landscape-scale Maw sign in the chapter; escalation from place-scale (Maharashtra's burnt nest) to landscape-scale
relationships: Shrine built same day at Assi Ghat by the Varanasi boatmen-guild on Gangaputra's order; stone and packed earth; single carved barasingha-hoofprint on the riverside face
notes: Mechanism: the Maw has read the Ganga and erased her silt-memory for one full day, Assi Ghat to Manikarnika Ghat. The river runs glass-clear; the river-bottom is visible from boat to bank. Returns to muddy at sunset exactly. The shrine remains. UP's contribution to the catalogue is the escalation pattern: persons (Karnataka, Goa) → place (Maharashtra) → landscape (UP). Next signs will be larger still — the catalogue is climbing scales toward the Council message.

name: Sutrakara
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the assembly speech)
key_role: The chapter's quiet hero. Reads the famine mortality-arithmetic correctly when all twelve courts cannot. Speaks at the assembly. Is ignored. Walks out. The father-daughter corridor conversation is the chapter's dharmic pivot. Becomes Dvadashashringa's official advisor in the new single-court emergency governance.
relationships: Daughter of Dvadashashringa (mother deceased six years prior of aneurysm); cousin to Yamunadatta of UP (their pigeon-letter friendship begins this chapter); raised by gallery-usher Mrs Bhattacharji as much as by her father; sister-figure to no one (only child); collects the twelve scattered solar-gold prong-tips of the broken Dwadash staff after the dissolution
notes: Twelve years old. Mathematics prodigy. Has been drawing diagrams of judges' speech-patterns since age eight. Per restructure §3 she is poisoned in Chapter Three by Adharma-Kendra's agents (survives but loses her speech). Per restructure §6 she becomes the first non-hero on the Grand Council in Chapter Four — Central's representative-by-witness, mute, the kingdom's living memory of what late-deliberation costs. Aranya-Devi (deputy CJ) becomes her political mentor.

name: Aranya-Devi
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (Court XI session) — promoted Beat 3
key_role: The one chief justice who voted with Sutrakara at the assembly. Promoted to deputy chief justice of the new single-court system. Effectively runs daily operations by week six.
relationships: Former chief justice of Court XI (Forest & Wildlife) — the only one of the twelve who had publicly questioned Adharma-Kendra's neutrality before the dissolution; mentored Sutrakara through Ch 2 evening tutorials in administrative law; survives Ch 2 and Volume I as Central's most trusted operational voice
notes: Fifty-seven. Wears handloom kurtas like her UP counterpart Vidura-Babu (with whom she becomes close federation-counterpart across Ch 3 and 4). Has been a forest-wildlife judge for twenty-two years — knows Kanha National Park personally, including the meadow where the motionless herd will stand. Her early skepticism of Adharma-Kendra is the chapter's one bright procedural moment.

name: Mahaguru Drona-of-the-Plain (refugee phase)
faction: Senior Scholar (refugee guest then public witness)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (arrives at Bhopal before dawn) — testifies at dissolution
key_role: Hunted south from Lucknow by Adharma-Kendra's agents for the Imambara testimony given last month. Arrives at Dvadashashringa's side-gate at 3 a.m. carrying the proof-satchel (photographs, bank records, handwritten coordination memorandum). Stays as Dvadashashringa's secret guest for six weeks. Testifies publicly at the court-dissolution assembly. The testimony exposes the Karnataka–Goa–MP villain-coordination network for the first time in the saga.
relationships: Same Drona as the UP entry; cross-kingdom thread continues; sheltered by Dvadashashringa; will continue south or east to escape Adharma-Kendra's pursuit — destination uncertain; flagged as uncertain into Ch 3 and Ch 4
notes: His MP testimony is the saga's first cross-kingdom-coordinated-villain confirmation by documentary evidence. The proof he carries (the handwritten memorandum) becomes a chapter-three exhibit at the Sanctuary convening. Whether he survives the Adharma-Kendra pursuit into Ch 4 is the chapter's open question.

name: The Motionless Herd (multi-creature sign)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (two weeks post-dissolution)
key_role: First multi-creature Maw sign in the chapter; escalation pattern continues — person → place → landscape → multi-creature
relationships: Sandstone-and-packed-earth shrine at the southern edge of the Sonf meadow clearing; single barasingha-antler carved in low relief on the eastern face (the direction the herd had faced); Kanha forest guards become permanent shrine-keepers
notes: Mechanism: sixty barasingha stand motionless for eleven days, facing east, not grazing. On the twelfth day they resume grazing. None of them remember the eleven days — observable as a blankness in their behavioural memory through the bond. The Maw lives in the gap between knowing-the-question and answering-it; the herd's collective question (about the human famine-deliberation above them) was suspended in that gap. The Karnataka rule holds — Dvadashashringa marks the place and does not retaliate. MP's contribution to the catalogue: a multi-creature, multi-day, behavioural-paralysis event. The escalation pattern is now: person → place → landscape → multi-creature → ?

name: Bhairavi-Aaee
bloodline: C (third sister of the Chandravamsha — unnamed in formal records)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the temple gate)
key_role: The lineage reveal. Biological mother of both Kamalavarna and Kama-Mara. Witness to the Mahavidya rite from the inner-altar doorway. Returns to wandering after the rite — promises to return to Kamakhya at every new moon while both daughters live.
relationships: Third sister of Devi-Maa (deceased political seat-holder) and Bhairavi-Naam (deceased Kamakhya matriarch); biological mother of Kamalavarna (by an unnamed Brahmaputra-bank tantric, raised by Bhairavi-Naam at the temple) and Kama-Mara (by a Tibetan-Buddhist tantric scholar, raised by the father); wandering ascetic for 35 years
notes: Sixty-eight. The unnamed third sister whose existence the Chandravamsha formal records had erased — she walked away from the line at 23 because the line had only two formal seats and rejected her tantric vocation. The Kalika Purana's footnote on the Mahavidya rite explicitly names the 'three-sister-line-with-one-wanderer' configuration as the only one that can perform the central invocation. She returns to Kamakhya in week 3 of Chapter Two because the matriarch's death has opened the rite-window and she alone knows the lineage truth. Visibly ages during the rite (the rite costs the witness, too). Walks away at dawn without being seen leaving.

name: Bhairavi-Naam (deceased)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (her death)
key_role: The catalyst death of the chapter. Aunt-mother to Kamalavarna and biological aunt to Kama-Mara. Knew the lineage truth for 38 years and honoured the secret. Died of cumulative rite-incompletion after four months of secretly attending Kama-Mara's Open Coven Mahavidya-fragment cycles.
relationships: Sister to Devi-Maa (the political-seat-holder, also deceased) and to Bhairavi-Aaee (the wandering ascetic); Kamalavarna's adoptive mother for 38 years; senior matriarch of the Kamakhya temple for 51 years
notes: Eighty-seven. Found dead in her temple cell in week two of Chapter Two, arranged by her own hand in the seventh sub-rite Bhairavi-cycle eastern-facing posture. The arrangement is her last message to Kamalavarna — instructing her to perform the rite she has been suppressing. Cremated at the Brahmaputra ghat per Chandravamsha custom. Honoured in the new manuscript-case annotation as 'the matriarch who chose the dharma over the institution.'

name: Tara-priya
faction: Open Coven → Saraighat Second Temple Site
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the ferry crossing)
key_role: The oldest of Kama-Mara's senior coven women. Carries the cross-temple memory: was a Bhairavi-Naam student before being expelled with Kama-Mara in Ch 1. Speaks the decisive line 'We will not bring our blades' at the message-receiving scene. Becomes senior administrator of the formal Saraighat second-temple-site under the new arrangement.
relationships: Was Bhairavi-Naam's temple student before Ch 1; expelled alongside Kama-Mara; co-founder of the Open Coven; her conversion (back into formal Kamakhya structure under the new co-priestess arrangement) is the moment the temple women trust the integration
notes: Sixty-one. Wears burgundy. Her cross-temple service makes her the practical bridge between the two priestess-lines. By Ch 3 she runs daily operations at the Saraighat second site under Kama-Mara's seat the way Aranya-Devi runs daily operations at Bhopal under Dvadashashringa.

name: The Reversed Brahmaputra + Kneeling Rhinos (double-mode sign)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (seventh hour of the Mahavidya rite)
key_role: First DOUBLE-MODE Maw sign in the chapter — landscape-scale event (the river) and multi-creature event (the herd) simultaneously at the same hour
relationships: Two shrines built: (1) Saraighat reversal-point shrine at the river-bank — sandstone, packed earth, single carved wave-line in low relief; (2) Kaziranga kneeling-meadow shrine at the eastern edge of the meadow — sandstone, packed earth, single rhinoceros-horn carved in low relief on the western face. Both shrines maintained by their respective ranger/ferry-crew communities.
notes: Mechanism: during the seventh hour of the Mahavidya rite, the Brahmaputra at Saraighat reverses its direction of flow for exactly one hour (recorded by ferry-crews, news-channel boats, and Geological Survey of India). Simultaneously, 114 one-horned rhinos at Kaziranga kneel facing west toward Kamakhya. They kneel for the full seven hours of the rite. None of them remember the seven hours. The Maw lives in the gap between the rite-moment-of-asking and the rite-moment-of-answering; the seven-hour gap of the rite itself is the Maw's window. The Karnataka rule holds — Kamalavarna does not retaliate, marks both sites. Assam's contribution to the catalogue: the first DOUBLE-MODE event — landscape + multi-creature, same hour.

name: Ka-Sngi (deceased)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the Nongriat bridge)
key_role: The catalyst death that breaks Meghanadi's silence. Ka Khadduh of Meghanadi's family's main house. Pushed off the Nongriat double-decker living root bridge by her half-brother Kong-Bah at 5:47 a.m. on a Sunday morning in week 3.
relationships: Meghanadi's sister-cousin and Ka Khadduh by birth-order in the family's main house; half-sister to the killer Kong-Bah by their shared mother's first marriage; eldest sister to Ka-Sienlyngdoh (now 12 and the future bond-bearer)
notes: Twenty-six. Met at the Nongriat bridge every Sunday at dawn for nine years as part of the iaroh-snong tradition. The 62-metre fall into the Umshiang gorge killed her instantly. Investigated as accidental fall on slippery monsoon root-surface — the killer walked free for three weeks until his capture at the High Court storm. Her funeral at the Nongriat bridge in week 3 is the same site as Meghanadi's funeral eight weeks later — two women of the same line in the same grave-water, eight weeks apart.

name: U-Khrawkmen
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (arrives at High Court 23 minutes after Meghanadi's death)
key_role: The saga's first non-bonded political inheritor. Holds the Megha-Maata seat by Meghanadi's explicit written wish; the clouded-leopard bond stays dormant with the line for Ka-Sienlyngdoh.
relationships: Great-nephew of U-Mawkynrew (his late mother's aunt who raised him); Meghanadi's six-year protege and second-hand on the settlement-framework drafting; will travel to Kamakhya at the new moon for counsel from Kamalavarna and Kama-Mara; cross-kingdom correspondent with Vidura-Babu of UP
notes: Twenty-eight. Wears a plain Mixed Council Mediator's wool-and-cotton coat. The first male inheritor of a matrilineal kingdom in Khasi history. His authority is institutional and explicit-wish-based, not bond-based. By Ch 3 he becomes joint political voice of Meghalaya alongside Ka-Sienlyngdoh (when she carries the bond); by Ch 4 he is a senior council voice in the NE Dominant federation under Moirangthem of Manipur. Per restructure §4 he holds the political seat while the bond is dormant — Meghanadi's invented regent-by-naming mechanism.

name: U-Mawkynrew
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the kitchen-door scene)
key_role: The Garo elder who breaks Meghanadi's silence. Co-author of the settlement framework with U-Khrawkmen. U-Khrawkmen's great-aunt and lifelong mentor.
relationships: Garo elder from Tura; raised U-Khrawkmen after his parents' 2018 landslide death; four decades a Garo-Khasi mediator; the kitchen-table conversation with Meghanadi is the chapter's dharmic pivot
notes: Seventy-one. Wears a Garo nokma's wrap in deep indigo. Has been preparing the one-sentence intervention for nine years. Survives Volume I. Becomes U-Khrawkmen's senior council advisor through Ch 3 and Ch 4; will travel to Kamakhya with him at the new moon and to the Sanctuary convening as part of his retinue.

name: Ka-Sienlyngdoh
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the funeral of her sister Ka-Sngi)
key_role: The twelve-year-old niece on whom the clouded-leopard bond will settle in Ch 3 Beast-Rising. Holds the Ka Khadduh birth-order claim of the eastern Khasi Hills branch.
relationships: Meghanadi's eldest sister's youngest daughter; younger sister of the deceased Ka-Sngi; cousin to Moirangthem of Manipur via the Chandravamsha matrilineal line (corrected lineage tree); future cross-kingdom correspondent with Yamunadatta of UP (same age, both thrust into roles too large) and Sutrakara of MP
notes: Twelve. Stands at the eastern edge of the Nongriat bridge during Meghanadi's funeral. Does not yet carry the bond — the clouded leopard returned to the eastern hills after the eulogy without approaching her. The bond will settle on her at the Chapter Three Beast-Rising when the leopard walks to her threshold. She is the future political-and-bond inheritor of Meghalaya alongside U-Khrawkmen; the kingdom's institutional regent-by-naming + cosmic bond-bearer arrangement begins with the two of them.

name: Ka-Rhang-Wat-Snie (The Dry Day of Grief)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (24 hours starting at 5:47 a.m. the morning after Meghanadi's funeral)
key_role: First anti-weather Maw sign in the chapter — the absence of monsoon rain in monsoon territory
relationships: Sandstone-and-packed-earth shrine at the Mawphlang sacred grove edge; single cloud-pattern carved in low relief on the western face; the grove's elder hill myna sings the dedication-song at opening; day added to state calendar as permanent annual observance by U-Khrawkmen's first formal order; ratified by Council of Matrilineal Elders + Garo Hills District Council + Jaintia Hills District Council in concurrent emergency sessions
notes: Mechanism: rain stops at 5:47 a.m. (the exact minute Ka-Sngi died at Nongriat eleven weeks earlier); no precipitation for 24 hours at Cherrapunji, Mawsynram, Shillong; clouds present at usual altitude/density but do not rain; hill mynas at Mawphlang silent for the same 24 hours; first dry monsoon day in Cherrapunji rain-gauges' 83-year history. The Maw lives in the gap between question and answer — Meghanadi's speech and death framed the question; the institutional answer (Mixed Council, U-Khrawkmen's inheritance) is still forming; the dry day is the gap made meteorological. Meghalaya's contribution to the catalogue: the first ANTI-WEATHER event — absence of rain in the wettest place on earth in monsoon. Seventh rung of the escalation pattern.

name: Sangaputra
bloodline: C (Bloodline C senior via father + Bloodline C junior via mother through Dzulevira's elder sister)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the night before the Loktak massacre — sneaks onto the phumdi)
key_role: Co-founder at age 8 of Moirang-Tandava — the new pause-school dance-form. The eight-year-old observer who watched the Sangai deer for 11 days and discovered what 60 years of formal scholarship missed. Witnesses the Loktak massacre from a reed-clump.
relationships: Son of Moirangthem (Manipur) and Ka-Memcha (Tangkhul-Naga, Dzulevira of Nagaland's elder sister); nephew to Dzulevira; cousin to Ka-Sienlyngdoh of Meghalaya (the future bond-bearer there, also 12); will travel to Ukhrul for a fortnight before the new moon at Dzulevira's request to be with his Tangkhul-Naga grandmothers; will meet Ka-Sienlyngdoh at Kamakhya when the leopard settles on her
notes: Eight. Has been studying Thang-Ta since age four. Watches morning drill from the temple steps every dawn. The reed-clump that saved his life at Loktak; the deer who did not flee him; the eleven days of observation; the one-sentence answer to his father's grief. Per restructure §3 he is positioned as a future bond-bearer alongside Ka-Sienlyngdoh (both age 12 in Ch 3) — the Northeast's next generation of paired-by-age, paired-by-cousin-line heirs. His own Sangai-bond Stage I will form when he turns 12; until then he is observer, not bearer.

name: Ka-Memcha
bloodline: C (Bloodline C junior — Dzulevira's elder sister)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (background) — active Beat 2 (during Moirangthem's grief)

notes: Twenty-four. The bazaar movement's reconciliation-voice. By Ch 3 he becomes the new school's lead teacher of urban-diaspora dancers — the bridge between formal Manipuri-Meitei tradition and the Bangalore-Mumbai diaspora's contemporary forms. Survives Volume I as Moirangthem's senior junior.

name: Leishemba
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the temple courtyard scene)
key_role: The bazaar-elder who urged Moirangthem to listen to the raw-dancers in week three. Her one-sentence invitation is the moment the chapter's central question gets named.

name: The Nine Dancers Killed at Loktak

relationships: Tonjam (54, lead choreographer) | Ratna-priya (47, female lead) | Manaobi (43) | Ngambom (41) | Bishorjit (38) | Inakhumb (35) | Sapam (33) | Lalit (31) | Bobby (27)

Each name has, beside it, the classical sequence the dancer was performing at the moment of death.

name: The Loktak Mouth (self-signing sign)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (night after the final duel)
key_role: First SELF-SIGNING Maw sign in the chapter — the Maw makes its own form on the surface of a lake. Eighth rung of the escalation pattern.
relationships: Sandstone shrine at the Loktak western shore where Captain Tomthing's helicopter flight-path met the formation centre; Manipur Biodiversity Board logs the formation as 'unexplained phumdi-cohesion event' in the official ecological record
notes: Mechanism: floating phumdis arrange into a closing-mouth shape (4-kilometre mandible-arc, second 4-kilometre upper-lip arc, two rows of teeth-like dense phumdi-clusters inside). Formation holds for 7 minutes; closes for 90 seconds; drifts apart by minute 13. Captured on Pawan Hans cockpit-video by Captain Tomthing; 11 million views in 12 hours. The Maw is no longer signing the gaps in dharma — it is signing its own mouth. The Maw has become able to be seen directly. Moirangthem reads the signal through the bond: the escalation has crossed into form-making; the Council must sit before the next sign.

name: Ka-Memcha (deceased — second appearance)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the Tangkhul Tribal Ceremony Grounds at Ukhrul)
key_role: Second catalyst-death recorded across two kingdoms (alive in Manipur Ch 2, killed in Nagaland Ch 2). Her death is the chapter's most cross-kingdom-mourned single loss.
relationships: Eldest of three Tangkhul-Naga sisters; married Moirangthem of Manipur 2019; mother of Sangaputra (8); Dzulevira's elder sister; her funeral is performed by Dzulevira alone in combined Tangkhul-Meitei rites; ashes split — Meitei brass urn to Imphal, Tangkhul clay pot at Ukhrul

The killing is by Tangkhul Senior Priest Khrumai-Sho; she is pushed into the ceremonial fire-pit during the fire-purification sub-rite second circumambulation; the push is witnessed by 40 elders, the state-police detail, and 2 apprentices; recorded on Mhabemo's satellite phone. Three kingdoms grieve: Nagaland (her birth), Manipur (her marriage), Meghalaya (Ka-Sienlyngdoh's aunt-by-marriage).

name: Khrieo-Mama
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (midnight visit at the Kohima state-office on day 15 after Ka-Memcha's death)
key_role: The 89-year-old Angami matriarch who pulled the 600-year-old Pre-Tribal Pact out of her floorboards. The single most important institutional intervention of the chapter — without her arrival the walk does not happen.
relationships: Eldest Angami matriarch of Khonoma village near Kohima; has kept the Pre-Tribal Pact under floorboards since 1985 (her grandmother kept it 1923-1985; her grandmother's grandmother kept it 1882-1923); speaks 7 of the 16 Naga dialects fluently; her granddaughters provide translation help for the other 9
notes: Eighty-nine. Wears deep-indigo Angami matriarch's wrap with seven brass arm-rings. Walked seven kilometres alone from Khonoma to Kohima at midnight carrying the clay tablet. Her four-day translation work makes the walk possible. Walks the first three valleys with Dzulevira (Tangkhul, Khiamniungan, Konyak); knees give out; rides in support-jeep for valleys 4-16. Becomes Dzulevira's senior advisor through Volume I. Reads the Python-in-Loop sign at Pochury village. Survives Ch 2 and Volume I.

name: Phinika
faction: Small Tangkhul — the chapter's quiet bridge
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (walk preparation
key_role: day 5)
relationships: The ash-renewal-attendant for the 27-day walk. Renews the mithun-fire ash on Dzulevira's body each morning. Her presence is the chapter's quietest institutional act — a young Tangkhul woman who chose to assist the walk that began at the place her elder sister-in-law had died.
notes: Small Tangkhul-Naga clan; her elder sister had been Ka-Memcha's close friend; volunteered for the role on day 3 of preparation; carries the mithun-fire ash in a small clay container in the support-jeep; renews the ash at every village-edge stop
column15: Twenty-eight. Wears plain undyed Tangkhul cotton during the walk. The chapter's quietest character; speaks fewer than 10 sentences across 27 days. Per Khrieo-Mama's recommendation she is admitted to the new Mixed Council secretariat as Dzulevira's personal-attendant-of-state — a role created for her specifically that did not exist before.

name: Mhabemo
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the Hornbill committee room)
key_role: Dzulevira's chief secretary for two years. Operates the satellite-phone-and-Sarus-pigeon mesh throughout the chapter. Records Khrumai-Sho's arrest-confession on satellite-phone audio (key evidence for the criminal case).
relationships: Lotha clan-line; trained at Indian Administrative Service academy; close working relationship with Dzulevira since the 2024 inauguration; cross-kingdom administrative correspondent with Vidura-Babu at UP and U-Khrawkmen at Meghalaya
notes: Forty-two. The chapter's institutional spine. Manages the entire 27-day walk's logistics. Survives Ch 2 and Volume I. Becomes the chief operational voice of the new Mixed Council inter-tribal communication mesh in Ch 3.

name: The Python in the Loop (self-cancelling sign)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the morning after the Pochury confrontation)
key_role: First SELF-CANCELLING Maw sign in the chapter — the Maw's form completes by destroying itself. Ninth rung of the escalation pattern.
relationships: Burmese python preserved in formaldehyde at the Pochury village-edge museum-shrine; tail-in-mouth configuration maintained; shrine becomes a pilgrimage site for state-government school-children whose teachers add the python-shrine to the Nagaland curriculum's Sixth-Schedule civic-education module within four months
notes: Mechanism: a 2.8-metre Burmese python has swallowed its own tail; the constriction has cut off its own breathing; it is dead in the loop. Khrieo-Mama identifies the sign from pre-modern tantric texts as the 'Uroboros-fail' — the form of self-cancelling logic. The Pure-Tongue's sixteen mutually exclusive purity-claims are this form; each tribe's purity argument requires every other tribe's purity-impossibility; the constriction cuts off the breathing of the whole. The Maw's previous form-making (Loktak Mouth) was an attempt at form; the python is the form that fails by completing. The Maw is testing whether form-making can be self-defeating. Significance: the Maw is no longer initiating; it is experimenting.

name: Jagannath-Bandhu
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (the final 800 metres at 11:46 p.m. Monday week 6)

Carries the standing-second-shoulder-harness at his standing-following-position throughout (prepared by the Mahala-Maharana carpenter-line at Jagannathi's pre-pull instruction for the collapse-contingency). Joins the pull-rope at the Gundicha Temple's 800-metre-mark at 11:46 p.m. Monday week 6 after Jagannathi's collapse at 11:43:11. The two pull together across the final 800 metres at ~1 metre per 28 seconds. The standing-arrival-threshold is crossed at 11:47:18 p.m. The Stage III stroke completes on Jagannathi's body at the threshold-crossing moment when his right palm joins hers on the pull-rope. Conferred the standing-East-Dominant-successor seat at the standing-amended-charter's ratification-day.
relationships: Standing-Suryavamsha-line junior-priest 2007-2026 (15-year apprenticeship); Jagannathi's standing-shadow at every temple-administrative session for 4 years (since 2022); cross-region Sarus-pigeon correspondent with Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata at Karnataka (southern-bloc Dominant), Pulakeshi-Babu at AP, Jagannathi (until her early-Ch 3 sacrificial death); inherits East Dominant seat in Ch 3
notes: Thirty-one. Wears standing-junior-priest cotton across Ch 2; transitions to standing-state-hero formal cotton at the standing-East-Dominant-successor investiture at the amended-charter's ratification-day. Per restructure §1 he inherits East Dominant in Chapter Three after Jagannathi's early-Ch 3 sacrificial death during the first Beast-Rising; carries the East Dominant seat through Ch 4. The first standing-Brother-of-Jagannath honorific-holder to inherit the kingdom-council's standing-state-hero seat in the standing-charter's 800-year-record.

name: Subhadra-of-the-Wood

Mishra on Saturday week 6 at 5:14 p.m. Walks behind the chariot at the 3-metre-rear position across the three-day pull with the Shabara wood-bearer community of ~2,700. relationships: Standing-Shabara matriarch since 1996; standing-Daru-Brahma neem-wood selection-administrator 1982-2026 (4 Nabakalebara cycles); cross-cult correspondent with Pati-Mahapatra Senapati (Brahmin) and Mahanayak Rama-Chandra Das (Sadhaba) at the standing-three-cult shared-procession; the kingdom-council's standing-Shabara-lineage-register's standing-senior-administrator

The kingdom-council's standing-living-archive seat is the kingdom's standing-second non-rotational standing-seat (after Tamil Nadu's Avvaiyar-the-Younger). Per Ch 3 plan she attends the Sanctuary as the kingdom-council's standing-living-archive-seat representative; her standing-Daru-Brahma neem-wood selection-discipline informs the kingdom-council's standing-three-cult-rotation-memory across Chapters Three and Four. Survives Volume I.

name: The Counterclockwise Konark Wheels
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (12:03 a.m. to 1:03 p.m. Tuesday week 7)
key_role: First reversal-direction Maw sign in the chapter. The Konark Sun Temple at Konark (65 km south of Puri), 13th-century-CE Narasimhadeva-I temple built as a colossal stone chariot with 24 wheels (each 3 m diameter, carved with spoke-and-axle precision; functional sundials; not designed to turn; carved from single blocks). The wheels have not turned since the 1255 CE consecration (771 years). At 12:03 a.m. Tuesday week 7 (~4 hours after Jagannathi's chariot completed the Rath-Yatra), the seven southern-face wheels begin to turn counterclockwise at ~1 degree per minute. No mechanical mechanism. Each wheel completes one full counterclockwise rotation across ~360 minutes; all seven stop at original positions at 1:03 p.m. Tuesday.
relationships: ASI on-site night-watchman D. Mohanty (54) at 12:06 a.m. first-confirmation; ASI standing-on-call senior officer Dr. K. Patnaik (58) at 1:14 a.m.; standing-Maw-sign-recognition cell at 4:11 p.m. Tuesday; paired with Assam's Reversed Brahmaputra as saga's 4th cross-region Maw-sign pair (direction-reversal)
notes: The Maw has demonstrated the capacity to turn carved-stone wheels of a 13th-century temple counterclockwise for 13 hours through no mechanical mechanism. Paired with Assam's Reversed Brahmaputra (the river that flowed east-to-west for 1 hour during the Mahavidya rite at Kamakhya) as the saga's fourth formally-recognised cross-region Maw-sign pair: direction-reversal. Both signs are reversals of standing-natural-direction. 18th rung of the escalation pattern. The first reversal-direction experiment at a standing-monument scale; the Maw can reverse both standing-fluid-systems (Assam) and standing-solid-systems (Odisha).

Wait.') at 3:08 a.m. Was struck by the Ranga disc at 3:10:11 a.m. at the standing-killing-velocity. Body fell at 3:10:11:8 a.m. Standing-cerebral-spinal axis stopped at 3:10:12.
relationships: Bloodline-D elder brother to Chittaranga; son of Lakshmi-Akka (the standing-dancer mother) and Veera-Rao (the standing gem-cutter-and-informant father); cross-departmental Cyber-Hyderabad / standing-Cantonment administrative-coordination correspondent during weeks 1-6 of Ch 2 (the standing-mirror-monitoring registry's standing-administrative-coordination cell's seat-holder)

Ashes scattered at the standing-Musi-river-mouth at 5:11 p.m. by Chittaranga as the standing brother's eldest-surviving-male. The standing-killing is the kingdom-council's standing-permanent-record under the standing-charter's family-killing provision. The saga's first formally-recognised standing-vessel-of-voice in the registry.

Per Ch 3 plan she serves as the kingdom-council's standing emergency-petition cell chief; per Ch 4 plan she manages the federation's cross-kingdom petition-protocol.

name: Ranganatham
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (the contest-protocol invocation at 5:56 a.m. day 47)
key_role: The 57-year-old kingdom-council's senior delegate-chair across the 7-district kingdom-council. The standing-protocol expert on the kingdom-council's contest-of-arms protocol (the standing dispute-resolution mechanism for two-century-dormant twin-claim disputes). Verifies Kalaniksha's under-armament-by-twin-choice clause at 5:58 a.m. on day 47 with the standing-guru Acharya Sundaram and Indira Krishnayya. Confers with the kingdom-council on the 1828 Vakulamatha contest's under-armament precedent. Grants the clause. Conducts the contest's standing protocol-administration at the plateau's centre.

Per Ch 3 plan he attends the Sanctuary as the kingdom-council's standing senior delegate-chair; per Ch 4 plan he becomes the federation's standing protocol-administration chair.

name: Naga-Kumar
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the 6:13 a.m. day 48 tide-line observation)
key_role: The 23-year-old Hamsaladeevi village headman's grandson who walks the eastern beach at 6:11 every morning. Discovers the 1-metre tide-line retreat at 6:13 a.m. on day 48. name: The Metre That Vanished at Hamsaladeevi
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (6:13 a.m. day 48)
key_role: First land-erasure Maw sign in the chapter. The Krishna river's mouth eastern beach at Hamsaladeevi village's tide-line has retreated landward by exactly 1 metre across the full 600-metre east-west breadth between sunset on the contest-day and sunrise the next morning. The displaced land is approximately 600 cubic metres of delta-soil. No storm; no flood; standard tide-cycle confirmed by the Hamsaladeevi observation-station's tide-gauge. Displacement confirmed across Sentinel-2, Landsat-9, Cartosat-3 satellite-imagery services. The displaced mass is not in the Bay of Bengal's nearshore sediment-cell. The mass has been erased.
relationships: The kingdom-council's autumn coastal-protection-protocol amendment is the kingdom's institutional response; the Maw-sign cross-region pair with Kerala's black coconut establishes the southern federation's standing pairing-protocol for catalogue-pattern-recognition; the Hamsaladeevi-village memorial is established at the autumn kingdom-council session under Naga-Kumar's shrine-keeper appointment
notes: The Maw has demonstrated the capacity to erase a unit of land from the kingdom's geography. The Maw is asking: 'if you cannot kill your own twin, can you keep your own delta?' The kingdom's answer: the delta is preserved by the same mercy that did not kill the twin; the mercy is the kingdom-architecture; the architecture is the autumn coastal-protection-protocol. Fifteenth rung of the escalation pattern. The first cross-region paired Maw-sign with Kerala's black coconut. The southern federation's pairing-protocol becomes the saga's standing catalogue-pattern-recognition method.

name: Sivakami-Acharyini
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (Achyutan's body retrieval at the Sea-Front Kalari)
key_role: The 29-year-old senior 108-form deputy who becomes the kingdom's first female 108-form grandmaster. Parashurama's elder brother's daughter. At the kalari since age 6. Trained at the level of the senior daily-teaching cadre since age 22. Retrieves Achyutan's body from the Sea-Front Kalari at 11 a.m. on the day of death. Drafts the kingdom-council's emergency amended Kerala-Kalari Charter jointly with Parashurama across 3 days. Conferred the formal grandmaster-title at the kalari's evening ceremony day 23 (the kingdom's first female 108-form grandmaster ceremony in recorded history). Provides Kannada-Malayalam translation for Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata during the entire 31-day teaching. Acting kingdom-council deputy across the transmission-period.
relationships: Daughter of Parashurama's elder brother (Bloodline-D senior kalari-line); Karnataka-Malayalam bilingual through undergraduate-degree second-language training; cross-kingdom Sarus-pigeon correspondent with Hampi-of-the-Bronze (Karnataka, 10) as the southern-bloc's cross-kingdom student-side-mentor pair; cross-school institutional correspondent with Kala-Hasta Menon's Sea-Front Kalari
notes: Twenty-nine. Wears the standard kalari-instructor cotton, dark blue, with the grandmaster's red-bordered sash from day 23 onward. The chapter's institutional pivot — the new daily-teaching seat-holder who frees Parashurama to perform the 31-day transmission. Her grandmaster-aspirant journal entry on day 23 ('Uncle is paying the years. The bond is bargaining with time. The bond is winning the bargain.') is preserved in the kalari-tradition's standing-archive box. Per Ch 3 plan she attends the Sanctuary as Kerala's grandmaster representative; per Ch 4 plan she is the southern-bloc's standing kalari-tradition voice. Survives Volume I.

name: Achyutan-the-Nephew (deceased)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the northern-gate departure)
key_role: The 37-year-old senior daily-teaching deputy who defected to the Sea-Front Kalari and died practising the 109th form. Parashurama's elder sister Lakshmi-Akka's son. Bloodline-A by his mother's line — the same Bloodline-A branch that supplied Hampi-of-the-Bronze, Krishnaveni of AP, and (through long-shared maternal-line ancestor) Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata of Karnataka. At the kalari since age 12. Mastered all 108 forms by 33 (second-fastest in the kalari's recorded history). Defected Friday of week 2 with mother's written consent. Compressed the 24-week phasing into 3 weeks of private practice. Died at 5:58 a.m. Sunday of week 3 at the public class's seventh-transition demonstration; cause of death: basilar artery vascular rupture during the central rotation (phasing-violation cited).
relationships: Son of Lakshmi-Akka (63, Parashurama's elder sister); first cousin to Sivakami-Acharyini (through their fathers — Lakshmi-Akka and Parashurama's elder brother were siblings); related to Hampi-of-the-Bronze through the Bloodline-A maternal-line ancestor 4 generations back; the kalari's death-certificate records the basilar-artery rupture with the specific phasing-violation
notes: Thirty-seven. The chapter's pivot-death. The kalari's death-certificate filed by his mother at the Idukki District Civil Registry the afternoon of the death. Cremation at the kalari's western grove at sunset same day. Mother lights the fire at 7:02 p.m. Per the amended Kerala-Kalari Charter Page Six, his name is read aloud at the Sea-Front Kalari's day-zero phasing-discipline session at every new cohort opening for as long as the school operates. The reading is the kingdom's permanent witness-record.

name: Lakshmi-Akka
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the consent-signature) — active through Beat 2 (the cremation)
key_role: The 63-year-old elder sister of Parashurama and mother of the deceased Achyutan. Bloodline-A by descent. Widowed since 2014. Signed the Sea-Front Kalari's family-acknowledgement-clause consent-form on the morning of Achyutan's defection. Said to her son the night before: 'If you do not learn the form, you will be a man who refused his own ceiling. If you do learn it and live, you will be the kalari's next generation. If you do learn it and die, you will be your mother's son who chose. I am the mother in either case. The choice is yours.' Lit the cremation fire at 7:02 p.m. on the day of Achyutan's death. Sat beside Parashurama at the eastern edge of the grove for 3 hours 20 minutes in silence. Walked back to Idukki with the cremation-urn the same evening.
relationships: Elder sister of Parashurama VII (the seventh axe-bearer); aunt of Sivakami-Acharyini; mother of the deceased Achyutan; Bloodline-A by descent — the same maternal-line that connects to Hampi-of-the-Bronze, Krishnaveni, and (through long-shared maternal-ancestor) Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata; will not return to the kalari for 10 more years
notes: Sixty-three. Wears the white widow-cotton with the kalari-tradition's small black-bordered shawl across her shoulders. Said at 10:58 p.m. as her son's ashes were sealed: 'Brother. The kingdom-council's amended charter. The bird-letter you sent to Karnataka in March. Both. Sign them. Tonight.' The autumn bird-letter she sends to Parashurama after her son's death (the only piece of correspondence she sends him across the next decade): 'Brother. The day-zero session was conducted at the Sea-Front Kalari this morning at five-thirty. Sri Kala-Hasta read my son's name aloud at the opening. I was present at the amphitheatre's western entrance. I did not speak to him. The reading was honest. The cremation-urn is at my eastern wall. Sign. Take care. — L.' The autumn letter is filed in the kalari-tradition's standing-archive box.

name: Indira Pillai
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the 6 a.m. telephone call)
key_role: The 42-year-old religious-and-cultural-practice registry officer-on-duty at the chapter's opening telephone call. Confirmed to Parashurama at 6 a.m. on the chapter's opening Tuesday that the Sea-Front Kalari's registration had been filed 23 March under the standard kalari-charter and that the registry's 30-day silence had approved the registration on 22 April. relationships: Kerala State Civil Service registry-line; cross-departmental administrative correspondent with the kingdom-council's chief-secretary's office; the registry's standing kalari-charter-amendment-protocol drafted under her elevation
notes: Forty-two. The chapter's institutional bridge between the original kalari-charter's silence-defaulting protocol and the new amended charter's active-review requirement. Survives Volume I as the kingdom's standing kalari-charter-administrator.

name: Govindan-Mama
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the dawn-paper delivery) — active through Beat 3 (Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata's arrival)
key_role: The 68-year-old senior gate-keeper of the kalari's northern gate for 23 years. Welcomes Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata at the gate on 17 April at 3:47 p.m. with the standard kalari-courtesy welcome.
relationships: Idukki family-line; his father had delivered the Manorama to Parashurama's guru; his grandfather had delivered it to his guru's guru — the kalari's standing 4-generation institutional courier-line
notes: Sixty-eight. The chapter's quietest institutional figure. Bows to Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata in the standard Kerala greeting; bows again when the Karnataka cousin leaves on day 31 with the form in his spine. Survives Volume I.

name: Krishnan-Nair
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (6 a.m. day 32 black coconut discovery)
key_role: The 58-year-old senior groundsman and grove-keeper of the kalari's western grove for 24 years. Cordons the offering-platform with a small saffron-and-white twine perimeter on Parashurama's instruction. relationships: Idukki-born grove-keeper; can identify each of the 23 coconut palms in the grove by trunk-shape and crown-fan-orientation; cross-kingdom Forest-and-Wildlife-Department correspondent with Sunita Reang (Tripura, pigeon-shrine-keeper) and Vanlalruati (Mizoram, two-headed-serow witness) and Tashi-Bhutia (Sikkim, panda-at-altitude shrine-keeper)

The chapter's institutional witness to the Maw's material-permanence experiment. Refreshes the saffron-and-white twine perimeter at every dawn for the 8-month observation period. Survives Volume I.

name: The Black Coconut at the Western Grove
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (6 a.m. day 32)
key_role: First material-permanence Maw sign in the chapter. A single coconut on the 7th coconut palm from the northern boundary of the kalari's western grove turns matte black overnight after the day-31 re-sealing of the 109th-form chamber. The blackness is uniform; the husk is not charred but matte-black; the flesh inside is also black but firm and faintly sweet; the water is clear. Across 8 months the coconut does not rot.
relationships: The mother coconut palm is approximately 47 years old, part of the kalari's original grove planted 1979 after the previous grove's monsoon-storm destruction; the coconut sits on a small stone offering-platform at the grove's centre, cordoned with a saffron-and-white twine perimeter refreshed daily by Krishnan-Nair
notes: Preserved at the grove's offering-platform for the 8-month observation period. The kingdom-council's wildlife-rehabilitation and agricultural-research cells run weekly mass-and-temperature measurements, monthly micro-organism cultures, and quarterly fibre-strength tests. The coconut remains stable across the 8 months. Will be jointly named by Parashurama and Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata at the autumn when the observation completes. The cross-kingdom naming convention becomes the southern federation's standing Maw-naming protocol. The saga's first material-permanence Maw event; the inverse of Tripura's brooding-pigeon stuck-behaviour; the two signs are paired across the South-and-Northeast boundary.

name: Triputra
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (the 9-day rescue coordination)
key_role: The 19-year-old ward who inherits the throne after Tripurari's abdication. Tripurari's formal ward since age 11 (after the 2018 Agartala drainage-system fire killed both his parents; the same fire Tripurari personally led the rescue operation for). Trained as engineer-apprentice and as classical-Bengali-Tripuri poet in parallel from age 12 — the dual training was Tripurari's explicit decision. Was at the Ujjayanta Palace southern-edge bridge-engineering workshop when the collapse began; workshop survived. Coordinated the 9-day rescue operation; pulled Tripurari out at 4:11 p.m. on day 9; personally retrieved the 18th Phayre's Langur body from the pocket-space at 4:30 p.m.; counted the 17 langur-clan bodies at the western-Mahua-grove garden-wall rubble at 6 p.m. the same evening. Inherited the throne at noon on day 23. Wrote the first poem of his reign at midnight on day 45 — the opening line ('The bridge falls; the bridge is rebuilt; the bridge between us is the rebuilding.') became the kingdom's permanent state-motto-after-the-collapse, ratified by kingdom-council 22-2 on day 47.
relationships: Foster-son of Tripurari (legally adopted in 2018); cross-kingdom Sarus-pigeon correspondent with the Margin-hermitage (full-moon-and-new-moon-pair correspondence with Tripurari, archived under Anjali Debbarma's seal at the Bhubaneswari Temple); cross-kingdom federation correspondent with Bilash-Babu (West Bengal, Agartala compact), Kamalavarna (Assam, Udaipur compact), Hmangaihi-and-Lalruatpuia (Mizoram, Dharmanagar compact); will attend the Sanctuary in Ch 3 as Tripura's formal representative
notes: Nineteen. Wears the new ceremonial cotton white-with-senior-chair-sash. The saga's first HOPE-NOT-HERO throne-holder. Per Ch 3 plan he is the federation's smallest-and-most-fragile-kingdom voice at the Sanctuary. Per Ch 4 plan he attends the Kurukshetra Council carrying engineering-and-poetry rather than bond-authority. The dual training Tripurari gave him (engineering + poetry) is the kingdom's institutional discovery: engineering cannot substitute for politics; engineering must be paired with poetry; the kingdom's permanent state-motto-after-the-collapse encodes this discovery. Survives Volume I. The Phayre's Langur line cannot be re-bonded in Volume I; Triputra's reign rebuilds institutionally, not bond-wise.

name: Vyasa-of-the-Margins
introduced_in: Ch 2 Interval (the 3 a.m. day-21 field-hospital arrival)
key_role: The saga's standing guru-figure for broken-bond heroes. Offers Tripurari apprenticeship in the Margin-hermitage's broken-bond-integration discipline. The walking is the destination — 19 days west to the hermitage. The Margins do not participate in federation-level political bodies; the Margins do not use money; the Margins do not write down what does not need to be remembered.
relationships: Cross-kingdom counsel through Sarus-pigeon correspondence with broken-bond heroes at the hermitage; will reappear at Ch 3 Sanctuary twice as Margin-counsel only (not voting; not federation-member); will reappear at Ch 4 Kurukshetra Council formally as Margin-guru registrar
notes: Approximately 60 (age estimates vary; the Margin-walker is not aged by ordinary metrics). The standard dress: plain undyed cotton knee-length tied with a cord at the waist; barefoot; wooden walking-stave 1.5 m long polished by many hands; long white hair tied in a single braid at the back. The Margins are the saga's standing institution for broken-bond heroes; the broken-bond registry opens with Tripurari as the first entry; the Margins will maintain the registry across Volumes 2 and 3. The Margins' correspondence with the kingdoms is at every full-moon-and-new-moon pair by Sarus-pigeon.

name: Tri-Yantra-Bheda
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the sabotage-proposal)
key_role: The rakshasa-engineer who designed the triple sabotage. Forged civil-engineering-vulnerability doctorate from a forged Singapore university; one of 14 forged senior-technical-credentials the wider villain-network has produced for cross-kingdom-coordinated saboteurs. Survives Ch 2 in the flying-fortress operations-cell.

Wears engineering-consultancy cotton; speaks Bengali fluently with the precise technical-vocabulary that a forged-doctorate consultant would use; passes for an ordinary cross-border engineering-consultant in any south-Asian city. The forged-credential profile is the saga's first documented technical-saboteur with a forged senior-academic credential; the saga's wider villain-network registry will identify 13 similar profiles across the next three chapters.

name: Apurba Saha
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the water-rights committee noon-break phone call)

The chapter's most-tragic human-error figure — his information-disclosure enabled the sabotage; he did not know; he is institutionally suspended but not personally guilty in the criminal sense. The kingdom-council's emergency-response cell's standing recommendation: institutional reform of consortium-confidentiality protocols (no kingdom-internal technical-vulnerability information to be shared with cross-border counterparties without prior kingdom-council clearance). The recommendation is ratified at the day-47 council session. Per Ch 3 plan Apurba returns to active consortium duties after a 2-year suspension; per Ch 4 plan he serves as the consortium's standing institutional-confidentiality-protocol advisor.

name: Subimal Roy
faction: Bharat-Yantra Engineering Institute → Emergency-Response Cell Deputy
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the water-rights committee meeting)
key_role: The Bharat-Yantra engineering institute's senior engineering-research-cell chair. Supervised Tripurari's graduate thesis 2009-2011. Filed the institute's standing concern ('The king solves equations the kingdom no longer recognises.') in the confidential-correspondence drawer 18 months before the chapter. Survived the central-Agartala collapse (was on the 2nd floor; moved from the 3rd-floor review-session 10 minutes before the collapse). Becomes deputy chair of the kingdom-council's emergency-response cell on Tripurari's explicit appointment from the field-hospital bedside day 9. Cast one of the 3 dissenting votes against the abdication. Placed the ceremonial sash on Triputra's shoulders himself at the day-23 swearing-in.
relationships: Twenty-three years at the Bharat-Yantra institute; Tripurari's graduate-thesis supervisor; the institute's senior leadership had been circulating the standing concern for 18 months without raising it with Tripurari directly; cross-kingdom engineering-consultant correspondent with Bilash-Babu's West Bengal structural-engineering compact in the rebuilding decade

name: Anjali Debbarma
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the water-rights committee meeting)
key_role: The Bhubaneswari Temple Heritage-Trust chair. Three generations of her family at the temple. Wrote the line 'The young king solves the equation. The young king does not see the temple.' in her notebook at the noon-break; did not show the notebook to anyone until day 40 when she submitted it as part of the kingdom-council's post-collapse review-documentation. Survived the Udaipur central-market collapse (the temple's inner-courtyard wall held; the outer-courtyard wall fell). Coordinates the cross-Kamakhya-Bhubaneswari religious-administration compact. Holds the seal for the kingdom's permanent state-archive at the Bhubaneswari Temple manuscript-vault — the standing-archive for all Margin-throne correspondence after the abdication.
relationships: Cross-kingdom temple-administration correspondent with Kamalavarna's Kamakhya office (the Kamakhya-Bhubaneswari joint-rite during the Udaipur rebuilding decade); standing archive-seal-holder for the Margin-throne correspondence (Tripurari's full-moon-and-new-moon-pair letters from the Margin-hermitage)
notes: Fifty-one. The chapter's standing institutional voice for the temple-tradition. Cast one of the 3 dissenting votes against the abdication (she argued the temple-tradition required a senior-bonded ruler; affirmed her loyalty to the new arrangement). Survives Volume I as Triputra's senior temple-tradition counsel.

name: Sunita Reang
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the pigeon-and-stone-egg observation)

Becomes the kingdom's standing pigeon-shrine-keeper at the Mahua tree under the kingdom-council's day-43 appointment. Refreshes the small memorial-stone's saffron-cord-and-feather at every dawn.

notes: Forty-six. The chapter's institutional witness to the Maw's stuck-behaviour experiment. Filed the daily incident-reports with the kingdom-council's emergency-response cell. Survives Volume I.

name: TR-IMP-1141 + The Serpentinite Ovoid
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (5:18 a.m. day 25)
key_role: First stuck-behaviour Maw sign in the chapter. Green Imperial Pigeon (mature female, banded 2022) lays a serpentinite stone egg (287 g; 13x the standard egg-mass) at the Ujjayanta Palace western Mahua-tree. The nest collapses under the weight. The mother pigeon returns to the empty branch and performs the incubation behaviour on the absent nest for 14 consecutive days. She does not eat or drink. Dies in the incubation-posture on day 39 at 5:47 a.m.
relationships: Mate (TR-IMP-1142) presumed dead in the eastern collapse-zone, last sighted day 3 of recovery operations; the bird's body and the stone egg are preserved together in the zoological-museum sub-collection at the Agartala District Wildlife Office

Thirteenth rung of the escalation pattern. Krishnadevaraya-Bhrata's cross-region reply catalogues the three positions: presence-without-action (Karnataka's Bronze-Dust Child), future-naming (Mizoram's two-headed serow), stuck-behaviour (Tripura's brooding pigeon). The Maw is mapping the saga's response-space.

name: Lalruatpuia
faction: The Refusing Youth → New Political Seat
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the Aizawl Synod hall Manifesto address)
key_role: The 22-year-old Manifesto author who inherits the kingdom's political seat after his father's death. Drafted the spring 2025 first-draft Refusing Youth Manifesto.
