notes: Twenty-two. Wears plain Mizo wool blue-and-grey without clan-pattern (the Manifesto-style; deliberately dressed without his father's family-mark at the August address and at the funeral procession). Inherits the bamboo staff-spear Hnam-Tuk at the funeral procession by Ramdinmawia's spoken declaration. Carries the spear into the kingdom-council's Friday ratification session. By Ch 3 he attends the Sanctuary as Mizoram's joint political voice with Hmangaihi. By Ch 4 he is a senior council voice in the NE Dominant federation under Moirangthem of Manipur. Survives Volume I. The 22-year-old non-bonded male political-inheritor pattern mirrors U-Khrawkmen's 28-year-old non-bonded inheritance at Meghalaya, with one key difference: U-Khrawkmen's authority was Meghanadi's explicit-wish; Lalruatpuia's authority is the kingdom-council's emergency vote following his father's death.

name: Hmangaihi
introduced_in: Ch 2 Interval (the western trailhead on the entry-morning)
key_role: The 17-year-old niece who inherits the serow-bond. Tlangvala's eldest sister's daughter (mother died in 2018 landslide; raised at Tlangvala's household from age 9). Stayed at Tlangvala's household during the December 2025 sit-in's family-fracture. Was at the western trailhead with Lalruatpuia from 4 a.m. on the entry-morning; watched the mark form through her late father's Forest Department binoculars. Received the serow-bond at 7:53 a.m. when the wild serow walked down from Phawngpui's southern ridge and stopped at her right side. Stage I hoofprint formed on her right shoulder across 48 hours. The two-headed serow kid spoke her name at 23 hours' age, 4 minutes before its death. Drafts the cross-kingdom Sarus-pigeon cascade-alert on the death-day; alert reaches all 9 bonded-kingdom senior guardians by sunset.
relationships: First cousin to Lalruatpuia (by their mothers — sisters); orphaned of mother (2018 landslide) and father (deputy district forest officer, deceased 2020 from undiagnosed pancreatic cancer); raised at Tlangvala's household; will be the saga's youngest formal bond-bearer at her Stage I formation (17); cross-kingdom Sarus-pigeon correspondent with Ka-Sienlyngdoh (Meghalaya, 12, future bond-bearer once her threshold is reached) and Sangaputra (Manipur, 8, pause-discoverer); inherits her late father's Forest Department binoculars as her primary work-implement
notes: Seventeen. Wears plain Mizo wool with the senior tribal-council's neutral grey shawl. Per Ch 3 plan she attends the Sanctuary as Mizoram's bond-bearer alongside Lalruatpuia and Lalrinpuii. The 17-year-old female bond-bearer pattern parallels Pema-Chöden (Sikkim, 16, refugee co-administrator) and Ka-Sienlyngdoh (Meghalaya, 12, future bond-bearer) but Hmangaihi's bond has already settled (vs Sikkim's institutional-only authority and Meghalaya's dormant clouded-leopard). Survives Volume I. By Ch 4 she is a senior council voice in the NE Dominant federation.

name: The Locked Generation (629 youth)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the new-moon week of week 4 locking)
key_role: The 629 Mizos aged 15-22 from all 13 kingdom-villages who accepted Parvata-Asura's 'refuge from the inheritance' offer. Locked inside Phawngpui Mountain at the new-moon week of week 4. Released through the southern fissure at 6:35 a.m. on day 3 of week 11 across 11 minutes. None die inside. 47 are dehydrated and 3 are mildly hypothermic; none requires hospitalisation. The kingdom's permanent witness-record of the chapter.
relationships: Drawn from all 13 villages — 47 from Aizawl, 83 Lunglei, 51 Champhai, 38 Saiha, 29 Mamit, 44 Kolasib, 68 Lawngtlai, 77 Serchhip plus 192 from sub-village clusters and the Bangalore-Delhi-Chennai-Singapore diaspora; lead-walker through the southern fissure was Lalpianhlira, an 18-year-old Saiha refugee who recovers the Hnam-Tuk from the exit-path and returns it to Ramdinmawia at the western trailhead by 10 a.m. that morning
notes: Survived 7 weeks inside the mountain with rations provided by Parvata-Asura. The kingdom's care for the 629 across the next 12 months is logged in the public Sacrifice-Acceptance Registry's auxiliary section — they are the saga's first documented survivors-of-asura-confinement; the kingdom's standard psychological-recovery programme (developed jointly by the Synod and the Mizoram State Civil Service) becomes the template for the saga's wider villain-network kidnap-survivors recovery procedures across Volumes Two-Three.

name: Ramdinmawia
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the Youth Council elder-side commentary) — active through Beat 3
key_role: The 81-year-old kingdom-council senior chair whose last act was the joint-signature ratification. Senior chair since 1996. Moved the unprecedented 15-7 vote to formally request Tlangvala not return. Voted in favour of the reformed Manifesto's ratification (18-6). Resigned the chair immediately after the vote. Passed the senior-chair's ceremonial bamboo gavel to Lalrinpuii at 6:28 p.m. on the ratification Friday.
relationships: Senior tribal-council chair 1996-2026; attended every biennium of the Youth Council since 1971; mentor to Ramdinmawia-the-younger (his grandson, who becomes the Aizawl District Tribal Council Chair in Ch 3)
notes: Eighty-one. Becomes the kingdom's standing elder-advisor through Ch 3 and Ch 4 without formal council seat. Survives Volume I in private retirement at his Aizawl home, attended by his three children and seven grandchildren. His sixty-three-year-old elder-side commentary to Lalrinpuii at the August Youth Council ('The boy is right. He is also wrong. He is right that the creed is being misused. He is wrong about the kingdom's readiness to administer it.') is preserved in the Synod's oral-tradition archive as the chapter's most-quoted elder statement.

name: Lalrinpuii
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the elder-side Youth Council commentary)
key_role: The 66-year-old Aizawl Presbyterian Synod senior moderator who drafted the sacrifice-geography (kingdom watches from west, asura takes the east, bond walks down between the two). Ratified by kingdom-council unanimous vote the night before the Tuesday entry. Succeeds Ramdinmawia as the kingdom-council's senior chair at 6:28 p.m. on the ratification Friday. The first Synod-moderator to hold the senior-chair position in the kingdom's post-1972 history.
relationships: Senior moderator of the Aizawl Presbyterian Synod since 2015; cross-Synod correspondent with the Mizo Presbyterian diaspora networks in Singapore and Bangalore; will attend the Sanctuary in Ch 3 as the kingdom's administrative voice alongside Hmangaihi and Lalruatpuia
notes: Sixty-six. The chapter's most institutionally significant succession — the kingdom-council's senior chair is drawn from the Synod for the first time since 1972. Her elevation is the kingdom's evidence that the new administration of the creed will draw from both the tribal-council and the Synod institutional traditions. Survives Volume I.

name: Vanlalruati
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the two-headed serow birth observation)
key_role: Senior shrine-keeper for the Phawngpui Mountain Sanctuary. Observed the two-headed serow kid's birth and 23-hour lifespan from the six-metre observation distance. Recorded the speech-event on her body-camera audio at 1:58 a.m. on the death-day. Subsequently appointed by kingdom-council vote as the shrine-keeper for both the eastern-face mark's bier-base (refreshes the bend with a small saffron cord each morning) and the two-headed serow's zoological-museum sub-collection (authorised to display the preserved body to family-members of the locked-six-hundred-and-twenty-nine on request).
relationships: Senior ranger Mizoram Forest Department since 2008; cross-kingdom Forest-Department correspondent with Tashi-Bhutia (Sikkim, Khangchendzonga panda-at-altitude shrine-keeper) and the Kanha forest-guards (the MP motionless-herd shrine-keepers); part of the saga's standing Forest-Department-as-Shrine-Keeper network established across Chapter Two
notes: Forty-one. The chapter's institutional bridge between the bond-mark (on the mountain) and the Maw-experiment (the speech-event). Her body-camera audio recording is the saga's first authenticated audio-record of a Maw future-naming event. Subsequent audio analysis (run by the Mizoram State Civil Service's forensic-audio sub-unit) confirms the two heads' voices were sharply distinct and the sub-fifty-millisecond synchrony was consistent with two distinct vocal-tracts speaking in coordinated production. Survives Volume I.

name: The Two-Headed Serow Kid
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (3:02 a.m. on day 4 after Tlangvala's death)
key_role: First future-naming Maw sign in the chapter. A two-headed kid born to a wild serow doe at the Phawngpui southern meadow. Lives 23 hours. At 1:58 a.m. on the death-day both heads speak together in plain Mizo a single word — Hmangaihi's name — 4 minutes before death.
relationships: The mother stays at the village outskirts for 3 days after the kid's death; villagers leave food and water; she does not eat or drink; on day 4 she walks back up to the meadow and is not seen again
notes: Preserved in formaldehyde at the Aizawl District Forest Department's zoological-museum sub-collection in the configuration in which it died. Not on public display. Logged as 'Two-headed serow kid, Phawngpui southern slope, post-natal death at 23 hours, observed speech at 23 hours minus 4 minutes, single word, Hmangaihi.' The saga's first authenticated future-naming event — the Maw has demonstrated the capacity to name the next bond-bearer aloud through a creature that should not have existed and should not have spoken. Twelfth rung of the escalation pattern.

name: Tani-of-the-Veil
introduced_in: Ch 2 Interval (the morning after Baba Parashar's cremation)
key_role: First cross-faction-defector co-administrator in Arunachal Pradesh's history. The Galo-tribe medic who pulled 7 wounded soldiers off the Tawang river-stone in 2022 before losing the sight in her right eye to flying granite. Was with the night-cult 13 months as Asta-Asura's primary interpreter; fluent in all 4 cult working languages (Apatani-Adi-Galo, cave-Tibetan, Hindi, English). Named by Baba Parashar at the Tawang valley pass moments before his death (the cloud-speaker heard her name in the cloud-bank's morning report before she heard it herself). Drafted the 7-page Order of the Dawn-Shadow Temple registration document in a single 30-hour session. Lifted her veil ONCE at the consecration for 15 seconds — the kingdom's permanent television-and-radio record of the wound the Temple is the answer to.
relationships: Galo-tribe by birth (Aalo district); served Indian Army's Arunachal Scouts as battlefield medic 2018-2022; war-disability discharge 2023; cult-defector 2026; Temple translator from week 4 onward; cross-kingdom Sarus-pigeon correspondent with Pema-Chöden at Sikkim (parallel co-administrator pattern — both 16-29 year old women holding institutional office in kingdoms whose senior virtue has been amended/curved this chapter) and Mhabemo at Kohima
notes: Twenty-nine. Wears the night-cult's plain dark-grey homespun under the kingdom-translator's neutral wool over-coat from week 4 onward. The silver-clipped black wool veil at her right temple is retained as her permanent personal mark. Per Ch 3 plan she attends the Sanctuary as Udayagiri's co-translator — the Sanctuary's first medic-trained attendee and first cross-faction-defector co-administrator. Trains two successor-translators (one from each faction) during the 11-week build-out. By Ch 4 she is a senior council voice in the NE Dominant federation under Moirangthem of Manipur. Survives Volume I.

name: Baba Parashar (deceased)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the cloud-line consultation; the Tawang valley pass killing)
key_role: The Karna-shadow loss that consecrated the first Dawn-Shadow Temple. Udayagiri's mentor since age 12. Lived above the cloud-line at 4,200m on the Sela ridge's northern face for 41 years. Spoke to clouds. Read the chapter's situation through the northwest cloud-bank's curve and articulated the Dawn-Shadow Temple architecture as the kingdom's required answer. Descended below the cloud-line for the first time since 1985 to announce the Temple at the Tawang valley pass. Killed at 3:27:39 p.m. on day 3 of week 3 by an arrow (from the dawn-tribe's 23-year-old third-rank archer) and a bullet (from the night-cult's 31-year-old second-rank rifleman), fired without coordination. Predicted his own death the night before.
relationships: Last continuous cloud-line resident in the kingdom's recorded history (the discipline ends with him; he has no successor); mentored Udayagiri 19 years; cremated above the cloud-line at first light the day after his killing by Udayagiri and Asta-Asura together (the first joint act across the faction-line); ashes divided equally — half scattered above the cloud-line, half interred at the Tawang Temple's cornerstone
notes: Sixty-eight. Faded saffron robes, wool socks, no shoes. The saga's first ARCHITECT-MENTOR'S FORTY-ONE-YEAR WARNING — the senior figure who descends from a kingdom's longest-running discipline once to articulate a kingdom-restructuring decision, knowing the descent costs his life. Saga-rule established here: the architect-mentor does not have a successor in their discipline; the discipline ends with them. The Tawang Temple's cornerstone is his body's interred half-ashes. The morning-greeting at all three Dawn-Shadow Temples (Tawang, Roing, Lower Subansiri) reads his name as the third invocation after the dawn-greeting and the Herald-naming (Sahodara-Aapun).

name: Tashi-Norbu
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the listening-floor scene with Asta-Asura)
key_role: The 2020 Galwan veteran missing his left arm below the elbow from the river-stone clash. First witness on the listening-floor to hear Asta-Asura speak. Stayed during Udayagiri's first conversation with the Comforter. After the chapter becomes one of the Tawang Temple's standing listening-floor caretakers — the cult's informal continuation under the formal Order's aegis.
relationships: Galwan-2020 veteran (Indian Army's Arunachal Scouts; same unit Tani-of-the-Veil served 2 years later); listened to the Comforter for 14 months; never formally joined the cult's senior delegate ring; was the cult's most quietly trusted long-listener
notes: Fifty-one. Wears a prosthetic left forearm-and-hand provided by the state-government's tribal-rehabilitation programme post-2020. Speaks Apatani-Adi-Galo and Hindi fluently; learned cave-Tibetan from listening to Asta-Asura's listening-floor pauses (a passive-acquisition fluency the cult-tradition recognises as legitimate). Survives Volume I; by Ch 4 he co-chairs the Tawang Temple's veteran-recovery sub-programme.

name: Sonam-Lama-Bumla
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the morning-council)
key_role: The senior administrative monk of the Tawang Monastery. Raises the night-cult agenda-item at the chapter's opening morning-council. Manages the Temple build-out's monastery-side logistics through 11 weeks. Counter-signs the 7-page registration document. Will attend the Sanctuary in Ch 3 as the kingdom's administrative voice (Udayagiri's third-position attendee alongside Tani-of-the-Veil and the Stage III bond-bearer himself).
relationships: Karmapa-Tawang lineage; no relation to Sonam at Rumtek (the name Sonam is common across the Karmapa-and-Tawang lineages); 9-year senior administrative monk at Tawang; cross-kingdom administrative correspondent with Lobsang and Sonam at Rumtek (the parallel name-pattern between the two senior administrative monks is noted but unremarked across the cross-kingdom record)
notes: Fifty-seven. The chapter's quiet institutional spine. Survives Ch 2 and Volume I. By Ch 3 he is one of the chief operational liaisons between the Tawang Temple's administration and the wider NE Federation.

name: Khoda-Jaya
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the Lower Subansiri pigeon-letter)
key_role: The 600-member Lower Subansiri sub-cult's senior delegate. Drafted the Lower Subansiri Temple admission-request 3 days after the Tawang consecration. Will become the Lower Subansiri Temple's shade-master at its 4th-month Ch 3 consecration.
relationships: Apatani-tribe; her name Khoda is from the Apatani creator-line and means 'the one who is brought forth'; cross-cult correspondent with Asta-Asura through the cult's old listening-floor pigeon-relay before the Tawang consecration formalised the network
notes: Thirty-eight. Wears the Apatani working-tunic. The first replication of the Temple architecture in the kingdom; will be the Lower Subansiri Temple's shade-master from Ch 3 forward. The Lower Subansiri Temple's dawn-master will be drawn from the Apatani-tribe-elder council (the council ratifying its appointment in week 1 of Ch 3) and the translator from the local medic-and-teacher community (to be appointed under Tani-of-the-Veil's remote supervision).

name: Karme-Bobo
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the Roing build-out begins)
key_role: The former Tawang-clash medic who moved from Tawang to Roing to manage the second Dawn-Shadow Temple's build-out — explicitly the Herald-return room. Reads the village-headman's incident-log every morning at 5 a.m. before dawn. Receives Yapum-Mihu's First-Herald naming on the third Thursday after the foundations are laid.
relationships: Galo-Adi mixed background; 2022 Tawang clash medic (was Tani-of-the-Veil's junior on the same Arunachal Scouts unit); relocated to Roing autumn 2026; appointed by Udayagiri and Tani-of-the-Veil jointly
notes: Thirty-four. The first dawn-master of the Roing Dawn-Shadow Temple (the appointment is made informally during the build-out and formalised at the Ch 3 consecration). Survives Volume I.

name: Yapum-Mihu
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the naming of the First Herald)
key_role: The 13-year-old Adi translator-in-training at the Roing Temple-site who named the First Herald 'Sahodara-Aapun' — the brother-without-self — from the Adi-creator-line's children's songs. The naming holds the place where the face was. Becomes the Roing Temple's standing translator at the Ch 3 consecration.
relationships: Daughter of the Roing village-headman; trained as translator-in-training under Tani-of-the-Veil's remote supervision; cross-kingdom Sarus-pigeon correspondent with Sangaputra of Manipur (both 8-13 year olds whose discovery is the kingdom's institutional turning-point) and Sutrakara of MP (the 12-year-old MP Court-witness)
notes: Thirteen. The saga's youngest Herald-namer. The Adi children's songs she draws on become part of the kingdom's official Order morning-greeting at all three Temples thereafter. Per Ch 3 plan she is positioned as a future cross-kingdom translator alongside Sangaputra and Sutrakara — the saga's youngest-generation institutional voices.

name: Sahodara-Aapun (The First Herald)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the consecration morning at Roing)
key_role: The saga's First Herald in Maw-hierarchy terms. A man with no shadow who walks the 800-metre length of the Roing village's main path at 6:57 a.m. on the consecration morning. Face cannot be remembered by any of the ~130 witnesses. Named by 13-year-old Yapum-Mihu three weeks later as 'Sahodara-Aapun' — the brother-without-self from the Adi-creator-line.
relationships: The first Herald is the Maw's most-direct manifestation in human form. He is the saga's First Herald in Maw-hierarchy terms (not chronological terms; chronologically Karnataka's Third and Goa's Second appeared first, but they are further from the Maw's centre). Per D10 the Roing Dawn-Shadow Temple has been begun explicitly as the room he will be invited to walk through, when he returns. The return-visit is expected within the Chapter Three timeframe.
notes: Plain Adi-tribe homespun cotton shawl, undyed, no clan-pattern. Barefoot. Carries nothing. The standard mid-morning sun angle of 32 degrees should cast a westward shadow of about 1.6 times his height. He casts no shadow. The dirt-path beneath his bare feet shows no shadow-track, no foot-impression, no compression. Within 90 minutes of his passage no witness can describe his face. The face has erased itself from the world's memory. The naming holds the place where the face was. The kingdom does not forget the forgetting.

name: Pema-Chöden
faction: The Refugees Themselves (Faction Three) → Co-Administrator (institutional first)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (the monastery east gate at 5:12 a.m. on day 47)
key_role: The first refugee in the Beyul-Kshetra's nine-century history to hold institutional office. Identifies the Refugee Father as Krodha from a coloured-pencil drawing she made at age 8 in 2018 in the actual Pelliang Village. Retrieves the Chintamani from the dawn-prayer-wheel at 1:06 p.m. on the boundary-speech day. Drafts the Pema-Chöden amendment (first amendment to the Compassion-Charter in 9 centuries).
relationships: Tibetan refugee from a village in the Chinese-occupied zone two days' walk west of Pelliang; parents (Tenzin and Dolma) and elder brother Wangchuk killed in the same border-crossing she survived at the autumn surge; intake-name registered as Pema-Wangchuk-Chöden so her brother 'keeps arriving in her paperwork'; surviving younger cousin Tashi-the-cousin (12, recovering at monastery rehabilitation-school); cross-kingdom correspondent through Lobsang-Mhabemo mutual-records exchange with Kohima
notes: Sixteen-and-three-months at the chapter's climax. Will be sixteen-and-five-months at the Chapter Three Sanctuary's scheduled date — the Sanctuary's youngest attendee and first refugee-attendee in three hundred years. Studies for the Sikkim state-civil-service junior-administrative-officer examination at Sonam's suggestion. Tutored by Lobsang (administrative-Tibetan), Sonam (state-administrative-Hindi), and the chief-secretary's deputy (state-government procedural protocol). Will receive a Khonoma-clay tea-bowl welcome-gift from Dzulevira at the Sanctuary opening. Per Ch 3 plan she becomes Sikkim's institutional voice alongside Kanchenjunga's bond-voice — saga's parallel to the U-Khrawkmen/Ka-Sienlyngdoh non-bonded-inheritor pattern but inverted (Pema is non-bond-bearing while Kanchenjunga retains the bond; in Meghalaya U-Khrawkmen is non-bond while Ka-Sienlyngdoh will carry the bond). She will not vote at the Sanctuary; she will be present as an aide. Survives Volume I.

name: Tashi-the-cousin
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 2 (referenced — the 12-day-old voice-substitution)
key_role: The 12-year-old whose voice was substituted by the Refugee Father's cadence during the evening sub-council. The recovery becomes the case-study for Lobsang's sub-council-recovery programme.
relationships: Pema-Chöden's younger cousin (her mother's sister's son); the surviving male of their family after the border-crossing; lives with Pema at south-camp barrack 22-A through Ch 2; transfers to monastery rehabilitation-school day 11 after the boundary-speech
notes: Twelve. The recovery takes time. He will recover. Begins speaking in his own voice again at week four of Lobsang's rehabilitation programme. Eleven other ex-sub-council boys enrolled with him. By Ch 3 he is a witness in the testimony-based reconstruction of the Refugee Father's recruitment-methods; his testimony helps shape the saga's understanding of Maw-adjacent psychological-implantation. Lives at the monastery from Ch 2 end onward; Pema-Chöden visits him at the school every Saturday afternoon.

name: Lobsang
introduced_in: Ch 1 references (intake-clerk for the 2024 Krodha registration); Ch 2 Beat 2 (the dawn-gate scene); Beat 3 (the 4-km key-run)
key_role: The junior monk who logged Krodha-Sherpa's arrival at intake-number 9,847 in 2024. Stood at the south side of the central altar during the autumn Refugee-Blessing Ceremony when the Refugee Father walked past him to adjust the butter-lamp. Runs the 4 km from the monastery archive to the south-camp eastern plaza in 45 minutes to deliver the dawn-prayer-wheel key to Pema-Chöden. Designs and runs the sub-council-recovery programme.
relationships: Karmapa-lineage monk ordained at age 24; intake-clerk for the south camp for seven years; one of three monks Kanchenjunga informs about the Chintamani theft (the other two are Sonam and the chief-secretary); becomes Pema-Chöden's administrative-Tibetan tutor
notes: Thirty-one. Carries the weight of the original intake throughout the chapter. After the chapter he becomes director of the monastery's new rehabilitation-school. Coordinates the Lobsang-Mhabemo cross-kingdom mutual-records exchange with the Nagaland State Government. Survives Volume I. By Ch 3 he is one of the chief operational liaisons between the Beyul-Kshetra's institutional administration and the wider NE Federation.

name: Sonam
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the silent search begins) — active through Beat 3
key_role: The senior administrative monk who managed the silent 47-day search across the monastery, the three south-Sikkim camps, and the surrounding villages. Carries the failed-search-discipline through the chapter as a quiet wound — the man who would have eventually found the Chintamani given another two months, but who was outpaced by a 16-year-old refugee girl walking 4 km with a memory drawn in coloured pencils 8 years earlier.
relationships: Karmapa-lineage monk ordained 1995; senior administrative monk since 2014; one of three monks Kanchenjunga informs about the Chintamani theft; becomes Pema-Chöden's state-administrative-Hindi tutor; files the mutual-records exchange with Mhabemo at Kohima within the same week as the amendment
notes: Fifty-four. Wears the senior administrative monk's grey under-robe with red over-sash. The forty-seven-day search is the longest sustained administrative operation in the Beyul-Kshetra's modern history. After the chapter he becomes the senior advisor on the new procedural-amendment institutional framework. Survives Volume I.

name: Tenzin-Norbu
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 3 (the senior monks council vote)
key_role: The second-most-senior monk after Kanchenjunga. Holds the Compassion-Charter as unamendable for 40 years. Casts the lone dissenting vote against the Pema-Chöden amendment (vote 23-1). Resigns from active senior-monks-council duties two days later in protest and takes up a meditation-cave residence in the central forest.
relationships: Karmapa-lineage senior monk for 51 years; Kanchenjunga's senior counsel since 2017; mentored both Lobsang and Sonam in their early ordination years
notes: Sixty-eight. The chapter's dissenting voice — the one who refuses the amendment on principle and accepts the majority will without obstruction. His retirement to the meditation-cave is a long-anticipated transition that the chapter's events accelerate by approximately two years. Survives Volume I in the cave-residence; Kanchenjunga and Pema-Chöden visit him together once a season for counsel.

name: Tashi-Bhutia
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (the panda-at-altitude sighting on December 2nd)
key_role: The senior ranger of the western-face patrol-station. Sights the red panda at five thousand four hundred metres on December 2nd at 7:43 a.m. during the standard December high-altitude wildlife-census. Becomes the permanent shrine-keeper of the Khangchendzonga Boundary Shrine at four thousand five hundred metres.
relationships: Khangchendzonga National Park senior ranger; 11-year park-service veteran; previously logged the 2022 panda conservation-tagging that identified the same individual at three thousand eight hundred metres; no relation to Tashi-the-cousin
notes: Forty-three. Wears the standard park-service olive uniform with the western-face patrol-station badge. Checks on the panda's grazing-spot through high-power binoculars once a week from the four-thousand-five-hundred-metre base camp. Does not climb higher. The panda has not descended in the months since the sighting. Survives Volume I as the ongoing shrine-keeper and the kingdom's standing witness to the Maw's species-lethal-altitude experiment.

name: The Red Panda at Five Thousand Four Hundred Metres (species-lethal-altitude sign)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Epilogue (December 2nd onward)
key_role: First SPECIES-LETHAL-CONDITION Maw sign in the chapter — the Maw shifts from form-making (Manipur, Nagaland) to direct experimentation on the saga's bond-architecture. Tenth rung of the escalation pattern.
relationships: Stacked-stone shrine at the Khangchendzonga western-face base camp at four thousand five hundred metres; single red-panda-paw-print carved in low relief on the eastern face; Park Service ranger Tashi-Bhutia as permanent shrine-keeper; weekly high-power-binocular monitoring from the base camp; cross-kingdom Sarus-pigeon cascade-alert sent to all 9 bonded-kingdom senior guardians by sunset of the sighting day
notes: Mechanism: a red panda is sighted at five thousand four hundred metres on Khangchendzonga's western face — six hundred metres above the species' documented maximum survival altitude. Red-panda haemoglobin lacks the high-altitude oxygen-affinity mutation; the species should die within 30 minutes from acute mountain-sickness combined with cold-stress at that altitude. The panda is alive, breathing at fourteen breaths per minute, grazing on a rhododendron-patch that has somehow survived six hundred metres above the rhododendron-belt's normal altitude limit. The ear-tag confirms it as a known Khangchendzonga National Park individual previously recorded at three thousand eight hundred metres. Observed for nine consecutive days; does not descend. The Maw is testing whether bonded animals can be sent to dwell at elevations that should kill them. If the panda lives, the Maw knows the bond is stronger than the species. The Maw will then begin moving other bonded animals to other lethal-to-the-species conditions across the saga's nine bonded kingdoms. Significance: the Maw is no longer reacting (Karnataka through Assam), no longer form-making (Manipur, Nagaland); it is experimenting on the bond-architecture itself. Sikkim's contribution to the catalogue is the tenth rung — the first species-lethal-altitude experiment.

name: Maitreyi-the-Younger
faction: Standing Nalanda-Order Acting-Mahasthavira + Standing Living-Archive Seat (NEW)
introduced_in: Ch 2 Beat 1 (the standing-Nalanda Reconstructed Library's standing-junior-librarian roster) — active through Beat 4
